Subject: Sudden spike in inference latency + 5xx on 'clinical-qa' route

Evelyn —

We started seeing increased tail latency and intermittent 5xx responses from the clinical-qa route at ~06:40 PT. P50 has jumped ~3x and p95 is above our SLA (we're seeing 600–900ms extra), plus ~8% of requests are returning 5xx. This is impacting our triage flow and flagging high for our on-call.

Can Redwood confirm whether this is a model/runtime regression or something in the network path? Our ops team saw a cluster of NAT timeouts and a handful of proxy 502s in the last 20 minutes.

We have execs on the bridge and need an ETA on root cause and mitigation. Please advise next steps and whether you want us to open a support tunnel.

Thanks,

Subject: RE: Sudden spike in inference latency + 5xx on 'clinical-qa' route

Quick triage notes (initial):
- Serving runtime: model processes are healthy, no OOMs, KV cache hit-rates unchanged.
- Token generation times per-step are normal for the variant in use.
- Networking: we see a correlated spike in TCP retransmits and SYN retries for the Peregrine peering CIDR in our egress region between 06:35–07:05 PT.
- Proxy layer: our edge proxy emitted sporadic 502/504 errors tied to connection resets; these co-occur with short DNS resolution failures to Peregrine's NAT hostname.

Attached a short connection trace and candidate root-cause indicators (conn-trace-20250519.txt). Early hypothesis: transient VPC peering route churn combined with an overloaded proxy instance in the egress fleet -> causes connection resets and DNS resolution fallbacks that surface as 5xx for the customer.

Immediate mitigations we can attempt (in order):
1) Bypass proxy for Peregrine's peering CIDR (quick config flip). Low risk, fast (~10–15m).
2) Route traffic to alternate peering region (requires routing update and sync with Peregrine; ~30–45m).
3) Temporarily roll back to the previous model variant with lower throughput footprint (if network mitigations are slow) — this is a last resort because it impacts latency/quality tradeoffs.

I'll start with (1) and surface results. If bypass reduces 5xx immediately, we continue and then work on a stable routing fix.

Vivek
Sr. Director, Serving Runtime

Date: 2025-05-19T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Peregrine Health — urgent exec summary and ask (SLA/watch)

Team — bringing leadership up to speed. TL;DR: Peregrine is experiencing increased tail latency (p95 > SLA) and ~8% 5xx, starting ~06:40 PT. Customer-facing impact: inference calls in their triage service are timing out and generating errors; execs want an ETA and a remediation plan.

What we know:
- Serving runtime intact; no model regressions detected.
- Network indicators point to peering route instability affecting egress connections to Peregrine's CIDRs and a single overloaded proxy instance that amplified connection resets.
- Preliminary mitigation (Vivek): bypass the proxy for Peregrine's peering range. If successful, this should sharply reduce 5xx; follow-on work required for a durable routing fix.

Requested leadership actions:
1) Approve proxy-bypass for Peregrine immediately (low-risk, reversible).
2) Authorize immediate high-priority routing remediation and post-mortem resources (eng + network).
3) Provide guidance on customer credit / SLA messaging (Sales + Legal).

Desired customer message (for the bridge/board): short summary of actions in flight and estimated: mitigation in 10–20m if bypass works; full stable fix within 6–12h (depends on peering coordination).

Attaching the proposed roll-forward plan and our suggested customer note (proposed-rollforward-plan-20250519.pdf). I'll coordinate comms with Marissa.

Evelyn

Update: we flipped the proxy-bypass for Peregrine's peering CIDR at 12:20 PT. Immediate results: 5xx rate dropped from ~8% -> 0.7% within 6 minutes; tail latency moved back within SLA bounds for p95 on the clinical-qa route. We've left the bypass in place while network performs a controlled routing rehome to a stable peer.

Next steps/owners:
- Network: controlled rehome to alternate peering (owner: netops, ETA 4h).
- Serving: continue monitoring for any residual proxy-side errors (owner: Vivek/Rishi).
- CS/Comms: customer message drafted (owner: Marissa).
- Legal/Sales: prepare SLA/credit options and customer-facing language (owner: VP Sales + Legal).

Attachments: conn-trace-20250519.txt (evidence), proposed-rollforward-plan-20250519.pdf (customer note).

I'll run a short post-mortem with netops and share a timeline for the rehome and permanent mitigations.

Vivek
